transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

I came in because I’m having trouble following through on things I start. Like after audits or mentorship events, I’ll begin the follow-up items with every intention of finishing them, and then a few days later I realize the final email, review note, or form never actually got done. It’s been happening enough that it’s starting to worry me.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things that usually interest you?
Not really, no. I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed, and I’m still interested in the things I usually care about. It’s more that I get frustrated with myself when I don’t finish things.
Do you find yourself getting easily distracted or having trouble focusing on tasks, even when you're trying to concentrate?

Yes, definitely. If I’m trying to review an audit file, even a Slack message or someone talking outside my office can completely pull me off track. Sometimes it’s not even external — I’ll suddenly think about something like marathon training, and then I’ve lost the thread of what I was doing.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be moving or doing something, even when you're trying to relax or focus on a task?

Yes, I do. Sitting still through a long review can feel physically uncomfortable, like this pressure building up inside me. After a while I feel like I have to stand up, walk to the printer, or find some reason to move around.
Do these difficulties with focus and restlessness happen in other areas of your life, like at home, in social situations, or during personal projects, or are they mostly limited to work tasks?

It’s not just work, no. Work is where it’s most obvious because the stakes are higher. I’ve made mistakes or left follow-up unfinished, and it got to the point where a client review was affected. I’m honestly worried people are starting to wonder if I can handle the promotion.

But it happens at home too. My husband has had to take over bills and things I agreed to do because I just don’t reliably finish them. It’s embarrassing, but it’s not only a work problem.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble focusing or staying still even when you were younger, like in school or during activities as a child?

Yes, I think so. Even in elementary school, my report cards would say things like I was bright, but I lost assignments or rushed through things and missed small details. I also got reminded a lot to finish my work, and apparently I talked out of turn.

My mother still jokes that I could do well on a test but forget the project sitting in my backpack.
How long have these issues with focus, distraction, and restlessness been affecting you — have they been a consistent part of your life for years, or is this something that’s gotten worse recently?

It’s been part of my life in some way for years, but the point where it really started interfering noticeably was about a year and ten months ago. That was after I got promoted following the firm-wide award, and my workload and responsibilities became a lot harder to juggle. Since then it’s felt much more difficult to keep up.
